## Patents: TitleChain Patent Pledge, Schedule A

The Nash scoring process is part of the TitleChain patented process for decentralized title
transfer, which scores an asset's provenance. Under that process, a unique identifier is tagged
to the container that denotes the underlying asset. The identifier carries the asset's
origination, issuance, asset type, and state of title. The process is covered by U.S. Patent
No. 11,720,888 (issued August 2023) and its continuation, U.S. Patent No. 12,518,273 (issued
January 2026), both titled *Decentralized Title Transfer and Validation of Assets*.

These patents are owned by Pamela Norton and licensed exclusively and irrevocably to the
TitleChain Sovereign Purpose Trust, established by TitleChain Foundation, which holds the
license so the process stays protected for everyone it serves and can never be captured by any
company, sponsor, vendor, or licensee. Erise IP manages the filings with the USPTO.

The Nash M5Score is a Designated Method in Schedule A of the TitleChain Patent Pledge
(`LICENSES/TitleChain-Patent-Pledge-1.0.md`). Once the Pledge is adopted and signed, anyone may
implement Nash royalty-free, as long as they keep the Cyrus Purpose Covenant. Until then, patent
rights are reserved, and the Cyrus license grants no patent rights (Cyrus License Section 5).
